messages:
claire: Quick heads-up — py + ts publish finished a moment ago but the docs site still shows 0.12.2 :grimacing:
release-bot: publish job finished for redwood-sdk-py v0.12.3 and @redwood/sdk-ts v0.12.3. Artifacts uploaded. Attempted to update dist-tags; API returned 422 for tags update.
raj: 422 how? any error snippet from the publish job?
release-bot: error snippet from pypi step: `422 Unprocessable Entity: metadata mismatch: dist_tags` (see full log at https://ci.internal/redwood/jenkins/1234)
mike: I saw that earlier with a mis-synced package.json -> package.json version mismatch on the TS build. If npm fails to set `latest` we can manually set the dist-tag: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.3 latest`
emily: Docs team wants to publish release notes now. Should we pin the docs snippets to 0.12.2 until dist-tag is fixed? We don't want users pulling the wrong package with snippets or quickstart.
claire: Agreed — short-term pin in docs + note in release notes: "dist-tag update delayed, use explicit version or follow this thread"
raj: mike, can you try manual dist-tag update for npm and then a twine metadata re-try for PyPI? If PyPI won't accept tag update, we'll push a yanked-tag workaround (pin reference).
mike: Running manual steps now. For reference, twine tag isn't a thing — PyPI uses release metadata. Quick check I will re-upload package metadata with corrected `version` fields and then hit the API to set our internal pointer. Commands I'm running:```bash
# npm side
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.3 latest
# py side (rebuild metadata only)
python -m build
twine upload --repository pypi dist/redwood_sdk-0.12.3-py3-none-any.whl
```
release-bot: manual npm dist-tag command returned 200; npm dist-tag now points to 0.12.3. PyPI metadata re-upload attempt returns the same 422: server rejects 'dist_tags' field.
emily: Ok npm fixed. For PyPI, thanks — we'll patch docs asap to explicit `pip install redwood-sdk==0.12.2` in the quickstart and add a callout in the release notes explaining the temporary mismatch + ETA for correction.
claire: I'll make the docs change now and add a prominent callout. Can someone add a short line in the release notes about the pin and include this thread link?
raj: I'll add the release-notes blurb and run a quick smoke to ensure no broken snippets.
mike: PyPI team said it's an internal validation flag; they're looking into it. For now, dist-tag fallback is resolved for npm; py pinned in docs. Leaving ticket for follow-up: INF-4572.
claire: Thanks all — closing this thread once release notes are updated. :thumbsup:
